title: Functions
description: def, parameters, return values, and closures
theory:
### Defining behavior

Functions are first-class objects created with `def`. Type annotations document
intent (`def greet(name: str) -> str:`) but are not enforced at runtime unless you
add a separate checker. Default arguments are evaluated **once** at function
definition time—never use mutable defaults (`def bad(items=[])`); use `None` and
allocate inside the body.

### Flexible signatures

`*args` collects positional extras into a tuple; `**kwargs` collects keyword extras
into a dict. Use `/` and `*` in the parameter list to control positional-only vs
keyword-only arguments when designing stable APIs.

```python
def append_suffix(base: str, *, suffix: str = "!") -> str:
    return base + suffix


def summarize(title: str, *scores: int, **meta: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"title": title, "scores": scores, "meta": meta}
```

exercises.title: Basic Function
exercises.description: Create a function greet() that prints Hello. Call it in main.
hints: Print Hello inside greet before calling greet().

exercises.title: Function with Parameters
exercises.description: Create function greet(name string) that prints Hello, name. Call with "Alice".
hints: Format the greeting with an f-string or concatenation referencing name.
Call greet("Alice") after defining the helper.

exercises.title: Function with Return
exercises.description: Create function add(a, b int) int that returns a+b. Call with 3 and 4, print result.

exercises.title: Multiple Return Values
exercises.description: Create function divide(a, b int) (int, error) that returns quotient and nil error, or 0 and error if b is 0. Call with 10 and 3, print result and error.
exercises.starter_code:
def divide(a, b):
    return None if b == 0 else a // b
hints: Preserve the divisor guard returning None for zero denominators.
print(divide(10, 3), divide(10, 0)) lines up quotient then None.

exercises.title: Variadic Function
exercises.description: Create function sum(numbers ...int) int that sums all numbers. Call with 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and print the result.
hints: *nums bundles arbitrary ints into a tuple parameter.

exercises.title: Defer Statement
exercises.description: Create a function process() that prints "start", defers printing "end", and prints "working". Call it in main.
hints: try / finally guarantees the trailing print even after ordinary completion.
Emit start before working, tuck working inside try, finish with end in finally.
exercises.solution:
def process():
    print('start')
    try:
        print('working')
    finally:
        print('end')

process()

exercises.title: Closure
exercises.description: Create function makeAdder() that returns a function that adds to a running total. Create adder = makeAdder(), then call adder(5) and adder(10), printing both results.
hints: Return a nested function closing over mutable total.
nonlocal total is required before += mutates the outer binding.
Each call to adder accumulates returning running totals.
exercises.solution:
def make_adder():
    total = 0
    def adder(x):
        nonlocal total
        total += x
        return total
    return adder

adder = make_adder()
print(adder(5))
print(adder(10))
